# Data and EDA {#sec-data}

```{python}
#| label: eda-setup
from collections.abc import Sequence
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib as mpl
from IPython.display import Markdown
from matplotlib_inline.backend_inline import set_matplotlib_formats

from ryuk.eda.files import read_summary
from ryuk.eda.summary import (
    AttributePrevalence,
    CelebaDraw,
    DetectionStats,
    GroupStats,
    ImagesPerIdentityRow,
)
from ryuk.plotting import EDA_FIGURES, use_lab_style

# Quarto runs the kernel in report/, so the committed summary is one level up.
summary = read_summary(Path("../eda"))

use_lab_style()
# Figures sit straight on the white page: the style's paper tone is for screens, and the PDF is
# for print (the committed eda/figures/*.svg are transparent for the same reason).
mpl.rcParams.update({"figure.facecolor": "none", "axes.facecolor": "none"})
# Constrained layout already fits each figure to its drawn width, the 6.3 in text column; the
# inline backend's default tight bounding box would pad it wider than the column.
set_matplotlib_formats("svg", bbox_inches=None)

lfw = summary.lfw
val, test = (next(d for d in summary.celeba if d.draw == draw) for draw in ("validation", "test"))
min_size = summary.min_usable_face_size
pairs = {p.name: p for p in lfw.pairs}


def count(n: int) -> str:
    return f"{n:,}"


def pct(part: float, whole: float = 1.0, digits: int = 1) -> str:
    return f"{100 * part / whole:.{digits}f}%"


def degrees(value: float) -> str:
    """Whole degrees with their sign, a true minus when negative."""
    return f"{value:+.0f}°".replace("-", "−")


def both(first: str, second: str) -> str:
    """One value for the two draws when they agree, else both in draw order."""
    return first if first == second else f"{first} and {second}"


def detected(stats: DetectionStats | GroupStats) -> str:
    return pct(stats.detected, stats.images)


def excluded(stats: DetectionStats | GroupStats) -> str:
    return pct(stats.images - stats.usable, stats.images)


def group(draw: CelebaDraw, attribute: str, value: bool = True) -> GroupStats:
    return next(g for g in draw.groups if g.attribute == attribute and g.value == value)


def prevalence(draw: CelebaDraw, attribute: str) -> AttributePrevalence:
    return next(a for a in draw.attributes if a.attribute == attribute)


def px(stats: DetectionStats, quantile: str = "p50") -> str:
    """A quantile of the detected face size, in pixels to one decimal."""
    quantiles = stats.face_short_side.quantiles
    assert quantiles is not None
    return f"{getattr(quantiles, quantile):.1f}"


def at_least(table: Sequence[ImagesPerIdentityRow], k: int) -> int:
    return sum(row.identities for row in table if row.images >= k)
```

Ryuk measures its recognition models on two public datasets: LFW for verification and CelebA for open-set identification. This section describes both as Ryuk sees them, through the YuNet detector at its default settings (score threshold `{python} f"{summary.provenance.score_threshold:g}"`), and fixes the minimum usable face size the rest of the project uses. Every number and figure here is read from the committed `eda/summary.json`, which `ryuk eda` wrote from the raw data at commit `{python} summary.provenance.git_commit[:7]`.

## LFW {#sec-data-lfw}

LFW has `{python} count(lfw.images_per_identity.identities)` identities and `{python} count(lfw.images_per_identity.images)` images, spread very unevenly (@fig-lfw-images-per-identity). The median identity has `{python} f"{lfw.images_per_identity.median:g}"` image, only `{python} count(at_least(lfw.images_per_identity.table, 2))` have the two or more a matched pair needs, and the most photographed has `{python} count(lfw.images_per_identity.max)`. Ryuk uses LFW only through its published pairs lists, for verification.

```{python}
#| label: fig-lfw-images-per-identity
#| fig-cap: "LFW's long tail: identities with at least *k* images, on log axes."
EDA_FIGURES["lfw-images-per-identity"](summary)
```

View 1's `pairsDevTrain` (`{python} count(pairs["pairsDevTrain"].matched)` matched and `{python} count(pairs["pairsDevTrain"].mismatched)` mismatched pairs) and `pairsDevTest` (`{python} count(pairs["pairsDevTest"].matched)` and `{python} count(pairs["pairsDevTest"].mismatched)`) are for tuning pipeline choices. View 2's `pairs` list, `{python} count(pairs["pairs"].matched)` matched and `{python} count(pairs["pairs"].mismatched)` mismatched pairs in `{python} pairs["pairs"].folds` folds over `{python} count(pairs["pairs"].identities)` identities and `{python} count(pairs["pairs"].images)` images, gives the reported accuracy (@fig-lfw-pair-composition). In `{python} count(pairs["pairsDevTrain"].pairs_with_excluded_image)`, `{python} count(pairs["pairsDevTest"].pairs_with_excluded_image)` and `{python} count(pairs["pairs"].pairs_with_excluded_image)` pairs respectively, at least one image has no usable face; in View 2 that is `{python} pct(pairs["pairs"].pairs_with_excluded_image, pairs["pairs"].matched + pairs["pairs"].mismatched)` of pairs. #26 has to decide how those pairs are scored, since published LFW accuracies are over every pair.

```{python}
#| label: fig-lfw-pair-composition
#| fig-cap: "LFW's pairs lists: matched and mismatched pairs, and the identities and images each draws on."
EDA_FIGURES["lfw-pair-composition"](summary)
```

## CelebA draws {#sec-data-celeba}

The validation draw is CelebA's `valid` split, `{python} count(val.images_per_identity.identities)` identities and `{python} count(val.images_per_identity.images)` images; the test draw is its `test` split, `{python} count(test.images_per_identity.identities)` identities and `{python} count(test.images_per_identity.images)` images. The two share no identities. Both have a median of `{python} both(f"{val.images_per_identity.median:g}", f"{test.images_per_identity.median:g}")` images per identity and at most `{python} val.images_per_identity.max` and `{python} test.images_per_identity.max` (@fig-celeba-images-per-identity). #9's gallery rule needs at least `{python} summary.rules.min_gallery_images` images per identity, which `{python} count(val.gallery_candidates)` validation and `{python} count(test.gallery_candidates)` test identities meet before any exclusion; @sec-data-eligibility applies it again after.

```{python}
#| label: fig-celeba-images-per-identity
#| fig-cap: "Images per identity in each CelebA draw, with #9's gallery threshold marked."
EDA_FIGURES["celeba-images-per-identity"](summary)
```

#17's five attributes are counted per identity as well as per image, because the bias breakdown compares groups of identities (@fig-celeba-attribute-prevalence). Male and Young describe the person, and #10 gives an identity one of their groups only when at least `{python} pct(summary.rules.majority_agreement, digits=0)` of its images agree. On the validation draw `{python} count(prevalence(val, "Male").majority_with)` identities are majority male and `{python} count(prevalence(val, "Male").majority_without)` majority not male, leaving `{python} prevalence(val, "Male").mixed` mixed; Young is less clear-cut, with `{python} count(prevalence(val, "Young").majority_with)` young, `{python} count(prevalence(val, "Young").majority_without)` not young and `{python} prevalence(val, "Young").mixed` mixed. On the test draw `{python} prevalence(test, "Male").mixed` and `{python} prevalence(test, "Young").mixed` identities are mixed. A mixed identity gets no group for that attribute.

```{python}
#| label: fig-celeba-attribute-prevalence
#| fig-cap: "#17's attributes counted per identity in each draw: Male and Young by #10's majority label, the photo conditions by how many of an identity's images carry them."
EDA_FIGURES["celeba-attribute-prevalence"](summary)
```

Eyeglasses, Wearing_Hat and Blurry describe the photo and vary between one identity's images. On the validation draw `{python} pct(prevalence(val, "Eyeglasses").images_with, val.images_per_identity.images)`, `{python} pct(prevalence(val, "Wearing_Hat").images_with, val.images_per_identity.images)` and `{python} pct(prevalence(val, "Blurry").images_with, val.images_per_identity.images)` of images carry them, spread over `{python} prevalence(val, "Eyeglasses").identities_with_any`, `{python} prevalence(val, "Wearing_Hat").identities_with_any` and `{python} prevalence(val, "Blurry").identities_with_any` identities, and only `{python} prevalence(val, "Eyeglasses").majority_with`, `{python} prevalence(val, "Wearing_Hat").majority_with` and `{python} prevalence(val, "Blurry").majority_with` identities carry them on most of their images. The photo conditions therefore group images, not identities.

## Detection and the minimum usable face size {#sec-data-detection}

YuNet re-detects a face in `{python} detected(lfw.detection)` of LFW images and in `{python} detected(val.detection)` and `{python} detected(test.detection)` of the validation and test draws' images (@fig-yunet-detection-rate). The rate is not even across groups. On the validation draw it finds a face in `{python} detected(group(val, "Male"))` of majority-male identities' images against `{python} detected(group(val, "Male", False))` of the rest, and in `{python} detected(group(val, "Young", False))` of not-young identities' images against `{python} detected(group(val, "Young"))` of young; the test draw shows the same gaps (`{python} detected(group(test, "Male"))` against `{python} detected(group(test, "Male", False))`, `{python} detected(group(test, "Young", False))` against `{python} detected(group(test, "Young"))`). Photo conditions cost more: on the validation draw YuNet finds a face in `{python} detected(group(val, "Blurry"))` of Blurry images, `{python} detected(group(val, "Wearing_Hat"))` of those with Wearing_Hat and `{python} detected(group(val, "Eyeglasses"))` of those with Eyeglasses. Where it finds several faces, in `{python} count(lfw.detection.multiple_faces)` LFW images and `{python} val.detection.multiple_faces` and `{python} test.detection.multiple_faces` CelebA ones, the face whose box centre is nearest the image centre is used.

```{python}
#| label: fig-yunet-detection-rate
#| fig-cap: "YuNet's re-detection rate, the share of images with any face found, per dataset, draw and group."
EDA_FIGURES["yunet-detection-rate"](summary)
```

Face size is the short side of the centre-most detection's box. LFW's faces are larger than CelebA's, a median of `{python} px(lfw.detection)` px against `{python} px(val.detection)` and `{python} px(test.detection)` px in the validation and test draws, and CelebA's are tightly bunched: 1% of each draw's detections are under `{python} px(val.detection, "p1")` and `{python} px(test.detection, "p1")` px (@fig-face-size). #17's rule sets the minimum usable face size at the largest multiple of `{python} min_size.step` px that keeps at least `{python} pct(min_size.keep, digits=0)` of CelebA's `{python} count(min_size.detections)` detections over both draws. That is `{python} min_size.value` px, which keeps `{python} pct(min_size.kept)`; `{python} min_size.value + min_size.step` px would keep only `{python} pct(min_size.kept_at_next_step)`. The same value replaces the detector's provisional default, so it governs enrollment and the live monitor as well as evaluation.

```{python}
#| label: fig-face-size
#| fig-cap: "Detected face size, the short side of the box, per dataset, and the low end where the minimum usable face size is set."
EDA_FIGURES["face-size"](summary)
```

The head pose is rough: a generic face fitted to YuNet's five landmarks (@fig-head-pose). Two caveats bound it. YuNet pulls its landmarks towards upright on rotated faces, so every angle is biased towards zero, roll most of all. And zero pitch means the typical portrait's pose, not a measured level head, so only the spread of pitch and the differences between datasets carry information. With that said, the middle 90% of yaw spans `{python} degrees(lfw.detection.head_pose.yaw.quantiles.p5)` to `{python} degrees(lfw.detection.head_pose.yaw.quantiles.p95)` on LFW and `{python} degrees(val.detection.head_pose.yaw.quantiles.p5)` to `{python} degrees(val.detection.head_pose.yaw.quantiles.p95)` on the validation draw, so CelebA has more turned faces; the middle 90% of roll stays between `{python} degrees(min(d.detection.head_pose.roll.quantiles.p5 for d in (lfw, val, test)))` and `{python} degrees(max(d.detection.head_pose.roll.quantiles.p95 for d in (lfw, val, test)))` everywhere.

```{python}
#| label: fig-head-pose
#| fig-cap: "The rough landmark head pose, yaw, pitch and roll, per dataset. Biased towards zero; zero pitch is the typical portrait."
EDA_FIGURES["head-pose"](summary)
```

## Exclusions and eligibility {#sec-data-eligibility}

An image with no usable face, either no detection or only detections under `{python} min_size.value` px, is excluded before anything else (@fig-exclusions). That removes `{python} count(lfw.detection.images - lfw.detection.usable)` LFW images (`{python} excluded(lfw.detection)`), and `{python} count(val.detection.images - val.detection.usable)` (`{python} excluded(val.detection)`) and `{python} count(test.detection.images - test.detection.usable)` (`{python} excluded(test.detection)`) from the validation and test draws. Most had no detection at all; only `{python} lfw.detection.detected - lfw.detection.usable`, `{python} val.detection.detected - val.detection.usable` and `{python} test.detection.detected - test.detection.usable` had a face that was too small. #9's `{python} summary.rules.min_gallery_images`-image rule is then applied to usable images (@tbl-celeba-draws): the eligible identities fall from `{python} val.gallery_candidates` gallery candidates to `{python} val.eligible_identities` on the validation draw and from `{python} test.gallery_candidates` to `{python} test.eligible_identities` on the test draw. #27's galleries are drawn from them.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-celeba-draws
#| tbl-cap: "The CelebA draws from images to eligible identities."
rows = [
    ("Identities", lambda d: d.images_per_identity.identities),
    ("Images", lambda d: d.detection.images),
    ("Images with a detection", lambda d: d.detection.detected),
    ("Images with a usable face", lambda d: d.detection.usable),
    (f"Gallery candidates, {summary.rules.min_gallery_images}+ images", lambda d: d.gallery_candidates),
    (f"Eligible identities, {summary.rules.min_gallery_images}+ usable images", lambda d: d.eligible_identities),
]
Markdown(
    "\n".join(
        [
            "| | Validation draw | Test draw |",
            "|:--|--:|--:|",
            *(f"| {name} | {count(value(val))} | {count(value(test))} |" for name, value in rows),
        ]
    )
)
```

Exclusion follows detection's unevenness. On the validation draw `{python} excluded(group(val, "Male"))` of majority-male identities' images are excluded against `{python} excluded(group(val, "Male", False))` of the rest, and `{python} excluded(group(val, "Young", False))` of not-young identities' against `{python} excluded(group(val, "Young"))` of young. The groups #10's bias breakdown compares are also unequal in size before any recognition model runs: on the validation draw `{python} group(val, "Male").eligible_identities` majority-male identities are eligible against `{python} group(val, "Male", False).eligible_identities` not male, and `{python} group(val, "Young", False).eligible_identities` not young against `{python} group(val, "Young").eligible_identities` young (`{python} group(test, "Male").eligible_identities`, `{python} group(test, "Male", False).eligible_identities`, `{python} group(test, "Young", False).eligible_identities` and `{python} group(test, "Young").eligible_identities` on the test draw). Estimates for the male and not-young groups will rest on fewer identities; what that does to the breakdown is measured in #28, not here.

```{python}
#| label: fig-exclusions
#| fig-cap: "Images excluded for having no usable face, and the eligible identities that remain, per dataset, draw and group."
EDA_FIGURES["exclusions"](summary)
```

## Limitations of the data {#sec-data-limitations}

CelebA labels neither skin tone nor race, so the bias breakdown covers only its Male and Young labels and the photo conditions Eyeglasses, Wearing_Hat and Blurry; whom the recognition models fail by skin tone cannot be measured on these data.

LFW and CelebA are photos of celebrities, some of whom may be in the recognition models' training sets. If they are, the models have seen these identities before, which would flatter the verification and identification results; how much cannot be measured here.

The detector is skewed before any recognition model is. YuNet finds faces less often in the photos of majority-male and not-young identities and in blurred, hatted and bespectacled photos, so exclusion removes more of them, and the recognition models are only ever measured on the faces YuNet found. The bias breakdown has to be read with the detection rates above beside it.
